The primary language of Algeria is Arabic, specifically Modern Standard Arabic (MSA), which is used in official documents, education, and media. This dialect is a colloquial form of Arabic that incorporates elements from Berber, French, and Turkish, reflecting Algeria's complex history.

In addition to Arabic, Berber languages, collectively referred to as Tamazight, are also widely spoken. Tamazight was recognized as a national language in 2002 and an official language alongside Arabic in 2016. There are several Berber dialects spoken across different regions of Algeria:
